newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up on tight liquidity, election.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up on tight liquidity, election.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 40 basis points from a low prior close to 20.30 percent in early trade Thursday on what traders and analysts said were liquidity pressures and some remaining jitters ahead of imminent mid-term elections.
"Rates halted their downward trend mainly due to the elections and next Wednesday's central bank cutoff," a fixed-income analyst said.
Banks have until next Wednesday, July 9, to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with the central bank.
Another analyst said pre-election jitters were much less than expected.

Mexicans vote on Sunday for an new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City. Previously, Mexico City's mayor has been a presidential appointee.

Dealers said another reason for secondary rates gaining was less demand for paper, with most foreign capital inflow into Mexico switching to the stock market ahead of the July 4 holiday on U.S. financial markets.
"Foreigns stepped in in droves yesterday, but I don't think they will again today, and that will put pressure on rates," another analyst said.
Overnight rates on bank paper were also under slight upside pressure and had risen 20 basis points to 21.75 percent.
Liquidity of 1.168 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
